names.note: Read out of the Охридски пролог’s second heading for 10. децембар ст. ст., „Преподобна Ангелина и свети Јован деспот.“ — «Преподобна» is the rank, which BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 reads as `venerable` and which comes off the stored form, so the bare forename is the whole of what the heading gives her. The body prints no surname and no see; it calls her «Мајка Ангелина», Mother Angelina, as the name the people use, and «Мајка» is not a name form either. Measured before it was written: the key is eight characters, above the width the gate indexes, and no other folder in the corpus holds this string, so it joins no fold.

The calendar’s nominative from name link 2386, «Блаженная Ангелина Сербская», with the rank word «Блаженная» left off; the day’s line gives it in the genitive with the title, «Ангелины , деспотиссы Сербской». `fk.mjs` returns no other holder for «ангелина сербская».

death.note: Охридски пролог за 10. децембар ст. ст.: «Упокојила се почетком XVI века и прешла у царство бесмртно» — she reposed at the beginning of the sixteenth century. The interval is the first half of that century, which is the corpus’s own reading of «early» in a century display; the book gives no year, and none is inferred. The display is not the book’s own words because `date-display.test.mjs` wants a form `lib/date-display.js` parses whole, and the book’s phrase is quoted here instead.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 июля ст. ст. — «Прав. Ангелины , деспотиссы Сербской (XVI).»

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry. This is the Serbian despotess the folder already keeps, and the Russian calendar keeps her on A DIFFERENT DAY from the Serbian row: 1 июля ст. ст. here, 10. децембар ст. ст. in the Охридски пролог. Two churches, two days, one row each — the schema’s shape, and no row was moved. Her century agrees: the line prints «(XVI)» and the folder holds the early sixteenth. The grade DIFFERS AT ONE WORD: this calendar writes «Прав.», righteous, where the folder’s `types` read venerable and monastic off the Serbian reading. `types` was NOT changed — one grade at two words is not a disagreement about the woman — and the difference is recorded here. Name page 2386 heads her «Блаженная Ангелина Сербская», a third grade again, and the life index behind the entry WAS NOT OPENED. The day page prints a troparion and a kontakion under her name, both taken below.
Not checked: doxologia.ro’s calendar for the corresponding day (8 October 2026).
Not checked: saint.gr’s εορτολόγιο for the corresponding day (8 October 2026).

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.12.2025 (10. децембар ст. ст.) — „Преподобна Ангелина и свети Јован деспот.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. ITS HEADING NAMES TWO PEOPLE and its body tells one life, hers, so the entry is two folders and the other is `john-the-despot`; both carry this same heading as their quoted line, because the heading is what the book prints and neither name has a heading of its own. THE BOOK’S OWN CROSS-REFERENCE, which the entry closes with, is «в. 30. јул» — see 30 July. THAT PAGE WAS NOT READ: the Julian 30 July is one of the four July days this corpus holds nobody on, so there is no row anywhere to compare, and this is NOT a second-day note and claims nothing about what 30 July prints. WHAT THE ENTRY GIVES: that she was the daughter of Ђорђе Скендербег, prince of the Albanians; that she was the wife of Стефан, despot of the Serbs, the son of Ђурађ; that she bore his exile with him and shared every bitterness of his life in Serbia, in Albania and in Italy; that she brought up her sons Максим and Јован in a true Christian spirit; that after her husband’s death she was tonsured and gave herself wholly to prayer, to works of mercy and to the building and repairing of churches; that a faithful wife, an excellent mother and a perfect Christian, she earned in truth the name «Мајка Ангелина»; that her wonderworking relics rest with her husband’s and her sons’ in the monastery of Крушедол, «уколико нису од Турака уништене»; and that she reposed at the beginning of the sixteenth century. NO `locations`: Serbia, Albania and Italy are an exile the entry does not bound, and Крушедол is where the relics lie and not where she lived. NOT FOLDERS AND NOT LINKED, because the corpus holds none of them: Ђорђе Скендербег; Стефан the despot, her husband, for whom no Stefan folder in the corpus is this man — the Stefans it keeps with a venerated serbian row are the First-Crowned, the Tall, Milutin, Dečanski and Штиљановић; Ђурађ, her husband’s father, named in `joannicius-of-devic`’s own record as the despot Đurađ Branković but holding no folder; and Максим, her other son, whom the heading does not name and who therefore took no folder here. ONE `related` row, both halves, to her son `john-the-despot`, whom the heading does name. UPDATE, 8 October 2026 — THE 30 JULY PAGE HAS NOW BEEN READ, AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE DESCRIBES THE STATE BEFORE THIS COMMIT AND NOT THE SOURCE. The Охридски пролог for 30. јул ст. ст., civil 2026-08-12, https://www.pravoslavno.rs/index.php?q=citanja&datum=2026-08-12&prolog=1, prints as its fifth entry „Преп. мајка Ангелина, деспотица српска.“ and TWO SENTENCES: «Мошти њене леже у ман. Крушедолу (Види њено житије 12. децембра)» — her relics lie in the monastery of Krušedol; see her life on 12 December. SO 30 JULY NAMES HER, AND THIS IS THE SECOND-DAY NOTE THAT ENTRY'S «в. 30. јул» WAS WAITING FOR. The row is copied back verbatim under `replace_venerated` and only this note grows: the day stays the Julian 10 December, which is the page that prints her life, and she does not render on 30 July. **THE BOOK'S OWN CROSS-REFERENCE IS TWO DAYS OUT AND BOTH PAGES ARE NOW READ**: it sends the reader to 12 December, and the Прологue's 12. децембар page prints Spyridon of Trimythous, the hieromartyr Alexander of Jerusalem and the martyr Razumnik and DOES NOT NAME HER, while its 10. децембар page carries the heading this row quotes and her whole life. Nothing was moved on the strength of the cross-reference. IT NAMES HER AND NOT HER SON: the 30 July entry has no word of «свети Јован деспот», whose folder carries the same «в. 30. јул» and whose own note records that separately. The 30 July heading also gives a form this row's folder does not hold, «Ангелина» with «мајка» and «деспотица српска» — «мајка», mother, is how the book addresses a nun and «деспотица српска» is a rank and a country, so §6 leaves the same bare «Ангелина» the folder already stores and no new form was written. The Prologue prints no hymn on 30 July.

hymns.text: В тебе, мати, известно спасеся, еже по образу,/ приимши бо крест, последовала еси Христу/ и, деющи, учила еси презирати убо плоть, преходит бо,/ прилежати же о души, вещи безсмертней./ Темже и со Ангелы срадуется, преподобная Ангелино, дух твой.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 июля ст. ст., «Тропарь праведной Ангелины, деспотиссы Сербской», глас 8 — the common of a venerable woman with her name set into its last line, which is how the page prints it

english.text: In thee, O mother, that which was made according to the image was surely saved; for taking up thy cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by thy deeds thou didst teach us to despise the flesh, for it passeth away, but to care for the soul, a thing immortal. Wherefore thy spirit, O venerable Angelina, rejoiceth together with the angels.

hymns.text: Вышняго живота желающи сподобитися,/ нижнюю пищу тщательно оставила еси,/ и богатство твое расточила еси нищим,/ и Небесное богатство прияла еси,/ и по смерти нас освящавши,/ и чудеса твоя, всехвальная Ангелино, источаеши./ Темже твое успение святое почитаем, взывающе:/ радуйся, мати прехвальная.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 июля ст. ст., «Кондак праведной Ангелины, деспотиссы Сербской», глас 8

english.text: Desiring to be accounted worthy of the life on high, thou didst diligently forsake the food below; thou didst scatter thy riches among the poor and didst receive the riches of heaven; and after thy death thou dost sanctify us and pour forth thy wonders, O all-praised Angelina. Wherefore we honour thy holy falling-asleep, crying out: Rejoice, O mother most praised.
